reading_note: Four sign units in the order U, bracketed strokes (two brackets enclosing 2 x 4 strokes), heart; the catalogue counts four signs, so the bracket pair and strokes are two catalogue signs or the small top marks are one; the grouping is left to Q-0013. The object photograph A shows the same units mirrored, with the U as a tall stem with rounded top at its right edge.
field: below the text: a curved stroke rising to the right from below the heart toward the upper right corner (horn-like), and a band of oblique parallel ridges at the lower centre with a rounded mass at lower right
animal_identification: unicorn not confirmed: the curved stroke is compatible with a unicorn horn and the oblique ridges with neck folds, but no head, standard or body survives clearly; no trunk, tusk or ear is visible
animal_features_against_elephant: no trunk, tusk or hatched ear in the surviving field
break: lower part of the face lost below the ridged band

views: CISI 2 PDF 120 render, impression box 1450,2010,1800,2560 and object box 1020,1360,1400,1910 (mirrored); composite data/raw/2026-10-13-plate-checks/pages/M895-heart-field-imp-and-mirrored-obj.png
observation: Below the heart sign a single long curved stroke starts just below the heart and rises to the upper right corner of the face; below and behind its base a band of oblique parallel ridges runs across the lower centre, and a rounded mass lies at the lower right where the face breaks off. Read as a right-facing animal on the impression: the curved stroke is a single horn rising forward from the top of the head, the rounded mass the head, the oblique ridges the neck folds. No trunk, tusk, hatched ear or columnar leg is visible.
identification: unicorn (single forward-curving horn with neck folds), first reader, moderate confidence; the body, standard and legs are lost with the lower face
